name: Elixir: Phoenix + LiveView + Ecto/PostgreSQL, with Oban when needed
choose_when: Server-owned state and business rules dominate a connected product.
Phoenix conventions and OTP process lifecycles match the service requirements.
A relational store can also support durable background jobs.
avoid_when: The main deliverable is a platform-native mobile UI or offline-first client.
The application depends on a library, accelerator or vendor SDK unsupported by the intended Elixir deployment.
A small static site, simple script or CLI does not need a running web application.

alternatives: Plain supervised Mix application for non-web services
tools.reason: Coherent routing, contexts and generated application structure.
tools.limits: Phoenix is unnecessary for a CLI or a service without HTTP; preserve existing architecture.

alternatives: Installed-version HexDocs and maintained repository guidance
tools.reason: Discover dependency documentation and synchronize selected upstream usage rules for agents
tools.limits: Development-only tool; inspect installed-version options and review generated content. Preserve Phoenix-generated guidance by default. An explicit README-only repository may configure file: "docs/dependency-rules.md" in mix.exs and link it from README; this destination is an optional project convention, not an upstream default.

alternatives: JavaScript hooks for isolated client behavior
Separate TypeScript browser application over Phoenix APIs
tools.reason: Shared server-side business operations and interactive screens suit connected forms, portals and collaboration.
tools.limits: Offline-first state, high-frequency local interactions and rich canvas editors can justify a dedicated client. LiveView does not remove HTML/CSS or all JavaScript.

alternatives: Another Ecto adapter when an actual persistence requirement warrants it
tools.reason: Explicit queries, changesets and database transactions fit shared application data.
tools.limits: Changeset validation is not a replacement for database constraints or authorization; database operations and migrations need operational ownership. Current Ecto documentation deprecates Repo.transaction/2 in favor of Repo.transact/2. Follow the installed-version API and callback/result semantics; do not mechanically rename an existing transaction without tests.

alternatives: External identity integration for SSO requirements
tools.reason: Generated first-party authentication keeps application-owned code; contexts authorize operations.
tools.limits: Check permission both on mount/navigation and each operation. Test revoked access and reconnect behavior; magic-link delivery needs a configured mail provider.

tools.default: Oban with the existing Ecto/PostgreSQL database
alternatives: Another supported Oban SQL engine after engine-specific qualification; retain the existing datastore when it meets requirements
tools.reason: Persist jobs and enqueue alongside domain changes in one transaction.
tools.limits: Task is only for explicitly disposable work and does not satisfy crash-durable delivery. Oban engine support and guarantees must be checked against the selected version; Redis is not a shipped Oban persistence engine. Oban Pro is an optional licensed extension, not a replacement for persistence.

tools.reason: Test contexts, data invariants, denied access and server-side UI behavior.
tools.limits: LiveViewTest does not establish browser JavaScript, accessibility or visual correctness. Inline/manual job tests are not a production recovery simulation.

tools.reason: Exercise hooks, navigation, reconnects and actual browser behavior omitted by server-side tests.
tools.limits: Adds Node/package-manager/browser binaries and sandbox configuration; verify supported wrapper features. It is an editorial extension, not a Phoenix generator default.

tools.default: Mix formatter and compiler warnings; Credo when selected
tools.reason: Fast local feedback plus consistency checks; select checks appropriate to project size.
tools.limits: Static analysis does not prove domain correctness. Dialyxir adds analysis/PLT maintenance and is not a mandatory starter dependency.

tools.default: Hex audit + Sobelow, alongside permission tests
tools.reason: Hex reports retired packages and known advisories; Sobelow finds common risky code patterns.
tools.limits: Use the installed Hex version’s behavior. Scan findings need review; configure a non-zero Sobelow exit threshold and do not blanket-suppress findings. Neither proves the application secure.

alternatives: Containerized release when the host benefits
tools.reason: Package application and runtime with explicit migration/server entry points.
tools.limits: Build for the target OS/architecture and native libraries. Host choice, secrets, migrations, TLS, backups, restore and rollback remain separate responsibilities.

alternatives: Evaluate LiveView Native separately for an explicitly suitable connected client
tools.reason: Preserve native UI/platform ownership while sharing server-side domain operations.
tools.limits: Do not advertise Elixir as a complete native mobile default: LiveView Native’s inspected README uses release-candidate dependencies and platform-specific clients. Validate target support, offline behavior, accessibility and signing independently.

tools.default: README navigation + generated Phoenix agent guidance
alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Keep generated stack conventions available to coding agents
tools.limits: Preserve maintained repository rules; --no-agents-md is an optional project choice, not the Phoenix default.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Mailer adapters and test delivery fit generated Phoenix account flows
tools.limits: Configure adapter/client dependencies and sender credentials; keep test/local adapters in development only. Use Oban for required queued delivery; a Task has no durable retry guarantee.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Built-in upload configuration and consumption fit connected forms
tools.limits: Configure allow_upload limits and authorize attachment association; persist consumed files before temp cleanup. External storage integration and content validation remain application work.

alternatives: Preserve an existing compatible project choice
tools.reason: Local/distributed publication updates connected views and channels
tools.limits: Supervise PubSub and subscribe to scoped topics; authorize each subscription/action and test reconnect. PubSub is transient broadcast, not durable replay or a message queue.

setup_steps: Read README.md, mix.exs, mix.lock and runtime pins; preserve existing applications. This is a recipe, not executed setup evidence.

For a new project, choose an empty source directory in a local development workspace. Check elixir --version, mix --version, mix phx.new --version and actual PostgreSQL connectivity; install only missing prerequisites using official instructions.

Resolve and record a compatible Elixir/OTP pair and Phoenix generator. Generate with mix phx.new my_app --database postgres; honor generated guidance. Use --no-agents-md only when the repository explicitly adopts a README-only instruction policy.

If dependency guidance synchronization is useful, add usage_rules as a development dependency, configure selected rules in mix.exs and review mix usage_rules.sync output. Honor generated Phoenix guidance; configure an alternate file only for an explicit repository policy.
Enter my_app; configure development database credentials outside committed secrets; inspect and run mix setup. For API-only creation use the documented --no-html --no-assets options instead.
If accounts are required, run mix phx.gen.auth Accounts User users --live, then mix deps.get and mix ecto.migrate; review generated instructions and email setup.
If jobs are required, follow the installed Oban installation/migration instructions, supervise Oban and configure bounded queues; write idempotent workers and tests.
Add selected development/test checks only. For PhoenixTest.Playwright install its JS dependency and matching browsers, configure test endpoint and SQL sandbox as documented.
Run the checks below and actual browser flows. Fix failures in place, retaining logs; never regenerate over work to hide a failure.

For deployment qualification, follow Phoenix releases: generate release helpers, compile production assets and build a target-compatible release. Rehearse migration, startup, reconnect, job retry and backup/restore on the selected host before claiming production readiness.
Completion: record exact versions, lockfile, checks and observed flows in README-linked evidence; report untested deployment/mobile paths explicitly.
verification_commands: mix credo --strict  # only after installing/configuring Credo
mix sobelow --strict --exit low  # only after installing/configuring Sobelow; review findings
mix dialyzer  # optional, after Dialyxir/PLT configuration
mix phx.server  # interactive smoke check, not an automated assertion
MIX_ENV=prod mix assets.deploy  # release qualification, after production prerequisites
MIX_ENV=prod mix release  # after release configuration; not deployment proof

sources.title: Ecto current transaction API and semantics

open_questions: Does the product fit connected server-owned UI, or need a separate offline/native client?
Which account/tenant permissions and email recovery requirements apply?
Which work needs durable retries and duplicate-effect protection?
Which host, object storage, observability and backup/restore requirements apply?
